instructions: Would an experienced developer, new to this code, expect changing it to be slow or risky? Judge how hard it is to understand and change, and ignore formatting.
To understand this code, must a reader hold several conditions or changing values in mind at once, each affecting the others?
How hard is it to follow one path through this code from start to finish?
criteria: The path stays in one place and reads top to bottom.
Following it means tracking several branches or state changes.
Following it means jumping between distant parts while state keeps changing.

instructions: Does a single function or class here do several unrelated jobs that would be easier to follow apart?
Do functions here change state, or have other effects, that their names and arguments give no hint of?
Does this code work only if its functions are called in a particular order that nothing in the code enforces?
How much of this code is near-copies that would all need the same edit when behaviour changes?
criteria: A few small blocks repeat with slight differences.
Several sizeable blocks repeat, so one change in behaviour means editing each copy.
Most of the logic is copies with variations, and some copies have already drifted apart.

instructions: How much information is stored in more than one place and kept in step by hand?
criteria: Each piece of information lives in one place, or the code holds no state.
One value is cached or copied, and it is refreshed in a single obvious place.
Several values are copied or cached, and every writer has to remember to update each copy.
Copies are updated unevenly in the code shown, so some paths can leave them disagreeing.

instructions: How often are related items listed one by one, in several places, where a collection and a loop would do?
criteria: Related items are held in a collection and handled by a loop.
A small set is listed by hand in one or two places.
A larger set is listed by hand in several functions, so adding an item means editing each of them.
Nearly every function lists the same large set by hand, where a missing or misplaced item would be easy to overlook.

instructions: Do the same special numbers or strings appear in several places without a name?
Does this code defend against states the code around it shows can't happen, such as a nil check on a value that is always set, or a fallback for a case that never occurs?
Does this file hold code that nothing visible uses: unused functions, parameters or variables, branches that can't be reached, or code left in comments?
Does this code carry options, hooks or layers of indirection that have a single caller or a single implementation?
Is much of this code wrappers that hand their arguments on to something else and add nothing?
Are many of the comments noise: restating what the next line plainly does, narrating the history of a change, or addressed to whoever asked for the code?
Does this code catch errors and carry on without handling or reporting them?
Does this code contain debug output, placeholder implementations or unfinished scaffolding?
Would the names here leave a reader guessing, because they are vague, inconsistent for the same thing, or say something the code doesn't do?
After reading this file, would a developer still be unsure what it is for?
Is most of this plain declarations, simple accessors, configuration or data whose behaviour is obvious at a glance? Size alone doesn't make code complicated.
